title: Square a racked gantry beam by sliding both carriages onto their end stops together
instruction: Slide the gantry beam along its rails until both carriages touch their far end stops, then let go.
context: Squaring the gantry is a routine step when a 3D printer, a CNC router or a Cartesian robot is built or serviced: with the belts and bolts loose, the beam is run onto both end stops together so that it sits square to its rails, and only then is everything tightened. The beam rides on two carriages on two parallel rails. Pushed at one end only it turns in its play, the carriages bind on their rails and it stops short, so both ends have to be moved together, by two hands. Machines of this kind make the parts of robots; a robot that can square a gantry can help build and maintain them.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x away from the arms, y to the left); heights over the bench top. One fixed layout, nothing varies by seed. A base plate 300 x 420 x 10 mm fixed to the bench, middle at x 27.5, y 0, long edges along y. Bolted to it, two HIWIN MGN12 linear rails (12 mm wide, 8 mm high, 250 mm long, steel) along x from x 15 to x 40, at y -17 and y +17, each with a red end stop block (10 x 30 x 13 mm) at both ends; the far stops' faces at x 40. The gantry: a 2020 aluminium extrusion 400 mm long bolted across two MGN12H carriages (45.4 mm long, 27 mm wide, one on each rail), with an orange toolhead block 40 x 50 x 40 mm on the beam's far face at its middle; 0.8 kg in all. It starts racked: the left carriage's far face 80.0 mm from its far stop, the right one's 77.3 mm (the beam turned 0.455 degrees). The carriages have 0.25 mm of play a side on their rails, standing for a gantry whose belts and bolts are loose. Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start in their ready pose.
scoring: The score is the state at the end of the trial. Distance of a carriage from its stop: from the middle of its far face to the face of the far stop of its rail. Opening at a stop: the larger of the two distances from the stop's face to the two upright edges of the carriage's far face. 0.25: both carriages 25 mm or more nearer their far stops than at the start. 0.5: both within 5 mm of their stops. 0.75: both touching face to face, the opening at each stop no wider than 0.1 mm. 1.0: touching, the beam at rest and both grippers 3 cm or more from the gantry; held for 1 s the trial ends as a success. 0 otherwise, also for a carriage off its rail or past a stop (neither can happen on this fixture: the carriages wrap the rails and each rail has a stop at both ends). Real bench: a tape from each carriage's far face to its stop for the first two levels (55.0 and 52.3 mm or less; 5 mm or less); a 0.1 mm feeler gauge that enters neither opening, tried at both edges of both faces, for touching; the video for the release.
reset_notes: Slide the beam back and set it racked against two gauge blocks: 80.0 mm between the left carriage and its far stop, 77.3 mm at the right. Belts off or loose, carriage bolts loosened to the stated play.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX, contact and friction only: the gantry is one free body with no joint, brake or rule holding or slowing it. A real MGN12H carriage runs on recirculating balls in grooves along the rail; here each carriage is a channel that wraps the rail's head with 0.25 mm of play a side and reaches under it with two lips, so it cannot be lifted more than the play or come off sideways. Balls and preload are not modelled; a new preloaded carriage has no play, and the play here stands for loose belts and bolts. Friction between carriage and rail is 0.2 (assumed; to be measured by tilting the fixture until the gantry slides). Pushed at one end the beam turns from 0.455 to about 0.61 degrees and binds; under a hard push at one end (12 N and more) it creeps a fraction of a millimetre a second: a wedge, not a lock. The gantry's 0.8 kg is from catalogue masses and is to be weighed. Rail and carriage sizes are the maker's catalogue figures. The last millimetres before a stop show in a wrist camera's picture (about 6 pixels for 5.6 mm at 320 x 176) and not in the top camera's.
